title: Progressive Telemetry Degradation and Recovery Contract
author: Asha Patel
body:
Overview
========

This document defines a standardized contract for progressive telemetry degradation and automated recovery across Redwood Inference services. The goal is to preserve essential SLI evidence and incident detection capability while gracefully reducing telemetry volume and cost when ingestion budgets, downstream backpressure, or operational emergency conditions require it. The contract specifies: ownership, staged degradation levels, metric and trace priority tiers, safe minimum telemetry sets, implementation patterns, recovery and verification steps, and testing/rollback guidance.

Why this exists
---------------

- Telemetry ingestion and retention costs can grow non-linearly under heavy traffic and degraded runtime conditions.
- Naive bulk sampling or blanket retention drops can remove signals needed to detect and triage outages or correctness regressions.
- Operators need predictable behavior: when and how telemetry will be reduced, who is responsible, and how the system will restore full instrumentation.

Scope and applicability
----------------------

Applies to: all production services that emit metrics, traces, and prompt telemetry into Redwood’s central telemetry pipeline (metric names: redwood.*; traces prefixed redwood-trace). This includes hosting plane services, runtime shards, ingress proxies, and the console. This contract does not change data classification or PII handling — those remain under security-and-compliance policies.

Terminology
-----------

- Degradation Event: a condition that triggers telemetry reduction (examples: ingestion backlog > 90% for 10m, telemetry budget burn rate > 120% daily projection, or dependent system outage).
- Degradation Level (L1..L4): predefined tiers describing how aggressively telemetry is reduced. L1 = mild reduction; L4 = emergency minimal set.
- Safe Minimum Set (SMS): the smallest set of telemetry required for incident detection and SLO evidence.
- Telemetry Fence: per-service configuration that defines what can be disabled at each degradation level.

Contract Principles
-------------------

1) Predictability: every service must expose a telemetry-fence config (YAML) that maps degradation levels to actions.
2) Prioritization: telemetry is tiered into Priority A/B/C where A = critical SLO SLIs, B = supporting metrics/traces, C = high-cardinality debugging signals.
3) Conservatism: never drop Priority A signals. Priority B may be sampled. Priority C may be fully turned off at L3+.
4) Safety-first rollbacks: any automated degradation must be reversible and accompanied by health checks that ensure incident detectability hasn’t been lost.
5) Auditability: every change in degradation state must be recorded as an event (redwood.telemetry.degradation_event) with reason, trigger, and operator identity/idempotency token.

Degradation levels and actions (reference)
----------------------------------------

- L0 (Normal): no change. Full telemetry per service defaults.
- L1 (Constrained ingestion): apply adaptive sampling to Priority C and non-essential debug logs; enable batching of events; delay low-importance retention flushes by up to 1 hour.
- L2 (Sustained budget overrun): sample Priority B at 25% and Priority C at 5%; reduce trace span details (keep parent/child but drop heavy tags); truncate or compress large text fields (prompt bodies).
- L3 (Severe pressure): disable Priority C metrics and traces; emit synthesized summary metrics (e.g., p50/p99) instead of full histograms; collapse multi-line logs into single-line headers.
- L4 (Emergency minimal): SMS only. Streamlined set: all Priority A metrics, one representative trace per 60s per service (trace sampling key: redwood.sampling.l4), and aggregated prompt-rate counters (no prompt text).

Safe Minimum Set (SMS) - example
-------------------------------

The SMS for any inference-facing runtime should include: 

- redwood.slo.latency.p50, redwood.slo.latency.p95, redwood.slo.error_rate
- redwood.capacity.available_gpus and redwood.capacity.pending_requests
- redwood.runtime.queue_depth_per_shard
- redwood.telemetry.degradation_state (current L0..L4)
- A single sampled trace per minute containing top-level timing and error tags, per runtime shard
- Aggregated prompt throughput counters: redwood.prompt.requests.total, redwood.prompt.requests.failed

Configuration schema (example YAML)
----------------------------------

services:
  - name: inference-runtime
    owner: eng-serving-runtime
    telemetry_fence:
      default_level: L0
      thresholds:
        ingestion_backlog_percent: 90
        budget_burn_rate_percent: 120
      levels:
        L1:
          sample: 
            priority_b: 80  # keep 80% of B
            priority_c: 20  # keep 20% of C
        L2:
          sample:
            priority_b: 25
            priority_c: 5
        L3:
          disable: ["priority_c"]
        L4:
          sms_only: true

Operator event schema (JSON example)
-----------------------------------

{
  "event_type": "redwood.telemetry.degradation_event",
  "service": "inference-runtime",
  "level": "L3",
  "reason": "ingestion_backlog_percent > 95 for 12m",
  "triggered_by": "autoscaler-policy:ingest-shed-v2",
  "operator_id": "ops-team-rotation-3",
  "timestamp": "2026-05-12T10:04:23Z"
}

Implementation guidance
-----------------------

1) Each service must implement a TelemetryFence component that:
   - reads per-service fence YAML from config-store (S3/consul/parameter-store),
   - exposes an HTTP admin endpoint (/admin/telemetry_state) to report current level and event history,
   - integrates with the central telemetry controller (see below) to receive commands and report audit events.

2) Local enforcement should be as close to the emission point as possible (e.g., SDK instrumentation layer inside runtime binary rather than a sidecar) to avoid excess CPU/networking overhead.

3) Use prioritized sampling for traces: implement deterministic, sticky sampling keyed by service:shard:request_id to maintain follow-up ability. Sampling keys should be reversible to add targeted replays in controlled environments.

Central controller responsibilities
----------------------------------

- Evaluate triggers: ingestion queue backlog, billing burn rate projections, downstream availability signals.
- Compute recommended global degradation level and reconcile per-service fence constraints (do not recommend L4 to services marked as "restricted-sms" without operator override).
- Publish decisions on the event bus and to the audit index.
- Provide a read-only dashboard and API for SRE/owners to approve immediate escalations or rollbacks.

Recovery and verification steps
------------------------------

When a degradation event clears (triggers no longer met):

1) Controller issues a staged rollback to L0 across affected services: L4 -> L2 -> L1 -> L0 with minimum stabilization windows (default: 2m between steps).
2) Each service must execute readiness checks after each step: ensure metric emission for a canonical Priority A metric and at least one sampled trace within 2 minutes.
3) Controller verifies ingestion backlog and budget projection for a stabilization period (default 10m) before issuing the next step.
4) If any service fails a readiness check, controller pauses rollback and notifies owners with remediation steps.

Dashboards and alerts
---------------------

Minimum dashboards every service owner must maintain: 

- Telemetry budget burn vs projection (90/95/100% thresholds)
- Degradation state timeline with event drill-down
- SMS health panel: shows presence/absence of Priority A metrics and their last emission timestamp

Alert rules (examples):

- FIRE: telemetry.ingest.backlog.percent > 95% for 10m -> page oncall + escalate to eng-infra 2nd
- WARN: redwood.telemetry.degradation_state != L0 && any Priority A metric missing for 5m -> slack notify owners

Testing and runbook exercises
----------------------------

- Every service must include unit tests that validate fence config parsing and admin endpoints.
- Create a synthetic traffic test that simulates ingestion-backlog triggers to validate L1..L4 transition behavior in staging before any production rollout.
- Conduct annual "telemetry game day" where SREs and owners practice degrading and recovering one major subsystem. Document outcomes and update fences.

Privacy and security considerations
----------------------------------

- SMS must never include user prompt text or full request bodies unless explicitly allowed by data classification and with appropriate retention exemptions.
- All degradation_event audit records are retained for 90 days in the audit index and surfaced to security for forensic requests.

Ownership and responsibilities
------------------------------

- Service Owners: maintain telemetry_fence config, own SMS definition, respond to degradation events.
- SRE/Platform: operate the central controller, maintain dashboards and alerting templates, run game days.
- Security: review any service-level exemptions that allow SMS to include higher-sensitivity fields.

Rollout checklist
-----------------

1) Add telemetry_fence YAML to config-store for each service.
2) Implement TelemetryFence admin endpoint and test locally.
3) Register service with central controller and run end-to-end staging simulation.
4) Publish dashboards and alert rules.
5) Schedule a canary rollout (10% of traffic) with manual approval gates.

Appendix: Example client-side pseudocode (sampling)
-------------------------------------------------

// pseudocode - deterministic sticky sampling
function shouldSample(service, shard, requestId, priority, level) {
  if (priority == 'A') return true
  if (level == 'L4') return false
  key = hash(service + ':' + shard + ':' + requestId) % 100
  threshold = config.sampleThreshold[priority][level] // e.g. 5, 25, 80
  return key < threshold
}
